instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of “lobbyist” covers any individual who “contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses” and whose duties include lobbying, without any dollar minimum compensation threshold.

A principal must register only after exceeding $500 in a calendar year in nonexempt lobbying expenditures/obligations, and principals anticipating ≤$500 may file a verified statement that exempts them and their lobbyist from licensing/registration/reporting if true.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text defines “lobbyist” in § 13.62(11) using compensation and a 5-days communications test, but contains no lobbyist-definition trigger based on the lobbyist’s own lobbying expenditures.

Wisconsin requires principals (not lobbyists) to file expense statements under § 13.68, and while § 13.68(4) requires lobbyists to provide information to principals, the statute does not establish a lobbyist-side expenditure reporting regime or per-item disclosure threshold for lobbyists.

The statute’s only time-based de minimis relates to principal reporting exclusions (e.g., non-lobbyist employees devoting ≤10 hours per reporting period in § 13.68(1)(a) and (c)), not an exemption based on a percentage of an individual lobbyist’s compensated time.
